m4, pure EA, 50 uL; frozen V1/V2 prediction 4.246445655822754/9.866485595703125 mL. With selected 100-uL pure EA and 100-uL 1/1, this completes a solvent-loading comparison anchored by measured 50-uL 1/1 record 05532ff0857a33a604d0. Recent high-loading measurements 032d9fbb133dff53e005 and 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7 showed that the completion increase persists through 2/1 and 1/1. This boundary reference tests whether it also persists in pure EA.

m4, pure EA, 100 uL; frozen prediction 4.155679225921631/9.941041946411133 mL. The forecast differs little from selected 50-uL pure EA, despite the measured approximately 5-6 mL completion increases between 50 and 150 uL across several other ratios. Together with the selected matched 1/1 point, this tests a solvent-dependent disappearance of the loading association rather than assuming a common completion correction.

m4, 1/1, 100 uL; frozen prediction 4.543632507324219/15.087871551513672 mL. Measured 50- and 150-uL records 05532ff0857a33a604d0 and 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7 finished at 12.525 and 18.508 mL. This missing midpoint tests interpolation versus a loading threshold and supplies the matched reference for selected 100-uL pure EA. It constrains onset and completion independently.

m3, 10/1, 150 uL; frozen prediction 5.671726226806641/16.08408546447754 mL. The recent 100-uL measurement 8ba04fd976f536e8340b was 4.367/13.908 mL, substantially earlier than the 50-uL 10/1 record 8048dcef1d7c5237b474. This third loading tests whether the late low-loading observation extends to high loading or represents a restricted feature. The selected matched 20/1 point separates solvent response from loading.

m3, 20/1, 150 uL; frozen prediction 5.095015525817871/13.9072904586792 mL. At 50 uL, measured 60d0510d3f8c8d6644dd was earlier than matched 10/1, whereas at 100 uL c25aed72c162a62800ce was slightly later than matched 10/1 record 8ba04fd976f536e8340b. This completes the high-loading comparison and tests whether the forecast restores the 10/1-to-20/1 advance. It cannot establish reproducibility of the unusual low-loading record.

m71, pure EA, 100 uL; frozen prediction 11.076223373413086/13.886616706848145 mL. This is a pronounced predicted onset delay relative to selected matched 2/1. Measured m71 records ec71ea81bb34e0bf505e and a6fd9cae6e0672265c13 have much earlier onsets under different loading conditions. The matched pair tests whether this strong-solvent extrapolation is real in a long-chain dibromothiophene; quantile crossing is only a model-consistency warning, not evidence of error.

m71, 2/1, 100 uL; frozen prediction 3.434197187423706/10.045365333557129 mL. This supplies a fixed-loading reference for selected pure EA, whose forecast has a much later onset. Existing 1/1 and 5/1 observations ec71ea81bb34e0bf505e and a6fd9cae6e0672265c13 use 150 uL, so relying on them alone would mix loading and mobile-phase effects. The pair provides a direct constraint for an unusual sulfur-containing hydrophobic scaffold.

m9, 10/1, 100 uL loaded in PE; frozen prediction 4.837662696838379/11.411245346069336 mL. Pending d39245aac516fd38a15a differs only in loading-solvent identity, using DCM, and predicts almost identical completion. This directly tests that small solvent-identity sensitivity. The close loading-volume contrast measured in m168 records b8abc8f40545556f07e0 and 5ba8cead5a790ba93029 does not establish invariance to solvent identity.

m23, 2/1, 50 uL; frozen prediction 4.6100358963012695/13.587871551513672 mL. Pending 33fe75ab7a516644119f tests 2/1 at 150 uL. This supplement determines whether that predicted completion enhancement transfers to low loading and supplies a measured-reference solvent contrast.

m189, 2/1, 100 uL; frozen prediction 5.717063903808594/15.550331115722656 mL. This stronger-eluent anchor, together with selected 20/1, helps distinguish a smooth response from a localized 10/1 depression in a biphenyl aldehyde with sparse measured condition coverage.

m189, 20/1, 100 uL; frozen prediction 6.537405967712402/22.55742645263672 mL. This is the weaker-eluent side of measured 10/1 record 360c6a3ecab6fd4cb98e. Measured 2/1 and 20/1 midpoint-loading anchors 04e994913bc43aa60007 and 10f14f6ee69ba06bbe68 finish at 10.450 and 20.783 mL; measured 5/1 record 9333d130f52d80332cf0 is at 50 uL. hypotheses.content: For m4, the observed completion increase from 50 to 150 uL persists through 2/1 and 1/1, with increases of approximately 5.34 and 5.98 mL and onset advances of approximately 1.1 mL. Its loading-response shape and extension into pure EA remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent acquisition-time completion underestimates extended into stronger eluent while onset predictions were much closer. The new crossed conditions test the scope and shape of an endpoint-specific association instead of applying a common endpoint shift.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 100 uL, does 1/1 completion interpolate between the measured loading endpoints, and does the 50-to-100-uL completion increase persist or disappear in pure EA?

hypotheses.content: The previous proposal of a loading-independent 10/1-to-20/1 advance for m3 is weakened. The advance is observed at 50 uL, but at 100 uL the 20/1 endpoints are slightly later than 10/1. A condition interaction and record variation remain competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest measurement showed that a correction inferred from the low-loading 10/1 record did not transfer to 100 uL. A matched high-loading pair tests the extent of that failure and discourages learning a universal solvent reversal.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL, are 10/1 endpoints later than 20/1 as currently forecast, approximately equal, or earlier as at 100 uL?

hypotheses.content: m71's predicted large pure-EA onset delay may reflect unsupported strong-solvent extrapolation. Existing measurements have early onsets, but their different loading conditions do not establish the matched 2/1-to-pure-EA response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched pair can expose or confirm a substantial model response in a sulfur-containing, long-chain hydrophobic scaffold. This tests structure-solvent transfer beyond the more common hydrocarbons and oxygen-containing compounds in the pending batch.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 100-uL loading, does pure EA actually delay onset markedly relative to 2/1, or do both conditions retain the early-onset behavior suggested by nearby measured records?

hypotheses.content: m67 has a larger observed onset association with loading at 2/1 than at 1/1: increasing loading from 50 to 150 uL advances onset by approximately 3.63 versus 1.20 mL. Completion changes are smaller. The intermediate-loading response is unmeasured, and unrecorded variation limits a causal interpretation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two matched midpoint labels distinguish smooth interpolation from a loading threshold and constrain solvent-dependent onset behavior separately from completion. These relationships may transfer to other alcohol-containing rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 100 uL, does the 2/1-to-1/1 onset difference remain substantial, and where do both endpoints fall between their measured low- and high-loading values?

feedback_interpretation:
The m4 outcomes strengthened the loading-completion association: the 150-uL 2/1 and 1/1 measurements finished at 19.725 and 18.508 mL, historical underestimates of 5.127 and 5.626 mL. Their matched loading increases resemble those already observed at 5/1 and 20/1. I therefore extend the question to pure EA and measure one loading midpoint rather than continue searching for a weak-solvent maximum.
For m3, the crossed comparison weakened the previous loading-invariant reversal hypothesis. At 50 uL, 10/1 was later than 20/1 in both endpoints; at 100 uL, 10/1 was slightly earlier. The high-loading pair now tests scope, while leaving reproducibility of the low-loading 10/1 record unresolved.
The m115 pure-EA repeat finished at 13.258 mL, 4.071 mL earlier than the previous same-tuple measurement. Both midpoint records remain above the measured 50- and 150-uL completions, but the peak magnitude was not reproduced. I reduce confidence in a sharp deterministic loading maximum and do not spend another slot repeating it. For m118, lower-loading pure-EA completion was 11.775 and 11.442 mL, later than the 8-9 mL forecasts but still far earlier than the exceptional 41.550-mL high-loading 1/1 completion. This supports restricted scope, not a uniform strong-solvent correction.
The m138 5/1 label supports a localized 2/1 enhancement within the measured 5/1, 2/1 and 1/1 segment. In m127, the lower-loading pure-EA completion increase was only 0.383 mL, compared with 2.575 mL at high loading, weakening loading-invariant boundary transfer. I defer both families after those discriminating outcomes.
The largest new selected overestimate was m164 at 5/1: completion was 14.375 mL versus its historical 22.294-mL forecast. An independent chalcone strong-solvent label tests related-structure transfer without assuming a shared correction. The m203 and m198 pairs showed decreasing completion from 2/1 to 1/1, rejecting their forecast plateaus and reducing the need for further nearby labels now. The m168 loading-volume contrast was small, consistent with its forecast; the new m9 comparison instead tests loading-solvent identity. Separately identified CW feedback included both completion overestimates and underestimates, so I do not infer a global endpoint correction. All reported errors are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The 16 supplements add distinct condition tuples and complement the supplied 16 pending experiments. Three m4 labels complete a measured-reference solvent-loading comparison and locate the pure-EA limit of a repeatedly observed completion association. Two m3 labels test the extent of a recent transfer failure. The m67 midpoint pair supplies a second, chemically different crossed experiment focused on onset-loading interactions.
Exploration targets specific model assumptions. The m71 pair tests a pronounced predicted solvent reversal at fixed loading. The m23 point complements a pending high-loading measurement and tests a completion increase accompanied by earlier onset. Two m189 labels bracket its measured 10/1 condition and pending 5/1 condition, distinguishing response curvature from a local depression. The m9 supplement creates a direct loading-solvent contrast with a pending experiment. The chalcone point and ortho-amino ester pair add structural and solvent-response constraints relevant to other aromatic carbonyl rows.
These labels should improve generalization by identifying which conditional corrections transfer across loading, solvent composition and related structures, and which remain local or variable. Selection is based on expected learning value rather than large retention or wide elution intervals. Quantile spans, including zero lower onset quantiles and crossed quantile heads, are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Chemical expectations about silica and solvent strength motivate tests but do not override the observed nonmonotonic responses. The supplied pending 16 and these 16 supplements, with their supplied premeasurement predictions, are fixed before any new labels are revealed.
